routingApi.design: The shell has no addEventListener/history call of its own (grep over src/*.ts matched only a comment in mount.ts). The runtime dispatches the link click through onUrlRequest; update returns a Command whose execute is Navigation.pushUrl; pushUrl's 'foldkit:urlchange' is received by the runtime's programmatic listener and routed back through onUrlChange; the runtime's popstate listener does the same for back/forward. External URL requests are deliberately a no-op (model unchanged) so the shell never triggers a page load in tests.

happyDomBehaviourMeasured.probe: node --input-type=module with happy-dom Window (run from apps/runtime-ui-next; 2026-10-25)
findings: history.replaceState/pushState update window.location synchronously (pathname/length) and do not emit popstate, matching browser behaviour.
history.back() restores the previous entry synchronously and emits popstate asynchronously (observed within 50ms); the popstate test uses a real back() over two pre-seeded entries.
A manually constructed PopStateEvent also reaches window listeners, but is not used by the tests.
MouseEvent/CustomEvent are available; the runtime's document click listener intercepts the anchor, preventDefault, and dispatches the Internal UrlRequest.
History entries are same-origin only; tests use relative paths under http://localhost:3000.
happyDomBehaviourMeasured.caution: This is not a real browser: bfcache, scroll restoration, cross-document navigation, and the actual History API limits are not exercised.

unverified: Real-browser behaviour is unverified; all routing assertions run under happy-dom. No cross-document navigation, bfcache, scroll restoration, or history state payload is tested.
External URL requests are a deliberate no-op; no load/openUrl path is tested (avoids network/browser navigation in the shell). Same-origin link clicks are covered.
Route coverage is exactly the three required routes (index, /diagnostics/:id, not-found); query strings, hashes and nested route families are not routed/asserted.
The Document title is set per route but the tests assert rendered body content only.

R21's diagnostics API/UI acceptance (authorized bounded query, redaction, headers/CORS, etc.) is not implemented here; this slice gives the diagnostics page a route to live at. That work belongs to its own slice.
scope: Only apps/runtime-ui-next/src/**, test/routes.test.ts and evidence were written. The S14a mount test was left unchanged and still passes; no wrapper, package, root, lockfile, vendor or private file was touched.
